findings.issue: The delivery plan does not fit the competition calendar. Entrants' submissions close 30 Nov 2026 23:59 London time (VTC page, opened). Stage B is due 10 Dec, after that close, yet it carries the 11 Nov dual-reading cenotaph test, the board shadow sheet, block sensitivity and the tower-position sweep. So do M04, M07 and M08. The Stage A core is already over capacity: 28-34 dev-days plus 3-5 data days against about 34 person-days. The tool therefore cannot give VTC entrants the board deliverable the brief recommends (solar/shadow studies on four A2 boards).
findings.fix: Re-plan to the entrant calendar. Set a feature freeze around 16 Nov so entrants have two weeks. Move the board shadow sheet and block sensitivity into Stage A, and apply the cut list now: M02 exploration only, M03 for one date, M06 deferred. Mark every module that will not ship before 30 Nov as 'post-competition' in the canvas, and remove VTC claims for those modules.

findings.issue: The exception-grounds flag gets the evidence backwards. UDI (S07, opened today) states the approved exceptions as affordable or social housing, major public amenities such as public childcare, and significant city-building priorities 'such as the Hotel Development Policy'. It also says a motion removed section 6.2, the exemption for 100% social housing. The spec flags this UDI-supported claim as FALSE ASSUMPTION and replaces it with the unopened relay list (below-market rental, heritage conservation). It also drops the Hotel Development Policy example, which matters directly because the brief's programme includes a hotel.
findings.fix: Change the flag to UNVERIFIED (conflict between relay and an opened secondary source). In ExceptionFlags, carry 'city-building priority, e.g. Hotel Development Policy' with evidence verified_secondary (S07). Keep below-market rental and heritage conservation as unverified relay. Record that the s.6.2 blanket social-housing exemption was removed. Add a human-judgment prompt asking whether the hotel component could support an exception case.

findings.issue: The CDDG exclusion is misread. The CDDG page (opened 21 Oct 2026) says the CDDG 'does not apply in some areas', including Victory Square. That exclusion governs applications on sites in those areas, not receivers. The spec says the exclusion 'may change which document governs' the cenotaph. A CBD tower site is inside the CDDG scope, so the open question is whether the CDDG solar chapter (not yet posted) keeps the cenotaph protection.
findings.fix: Reword the flag and parameter: the CDDG applies to the tower site, and the 13 Nov gate must check whether the posted CDDG solar text keeps s.4.3.1. Send that question to cddg@vancouver.ca along with the clock and total-or-new questions.

findings.issue: The mirror check uses angular sectors, which does not work with edge picks or with eastern candidate blocks. On this grid the edge normals sit at about 45/135/225/315 degrees, so an edge-picked label can be up to 45 degrees off the true bearing, beyond the +/-30 tolerance. The 'good' criterion also hard-codes BC Place as SE. From a block near Waterfront station, BC Place bears about 175-180 degrees (my derivation from approximate coordinates), outside the 105-165 sector, so the check would wrongly block M02.
findings.fix: Test handedness directly. Take the sign of the cyclic order (triangle orientation) of three labels (Stanley Park, BC Place, Burrard Inlet) in the model frame and compare it with geography. A reflection reverses that sign whatever the tolerance. Centre any sector on the per-block computed bearing and widen it to at least 50 degrees for edge picks.

findings.issue: The envelope formula h = z_p + d tan(alt at azimuth p->c) leaves several cases unspecified. It does not say what happens when the sun never reaches that azimuth inside the window (the cell is then unconstrained). It does not say how several rule windows combine (minimum over windows). It treats cells as points rather than finite areas, and it ignores receivers on sloping terrain. The swept-hull method likewise assumes a planar receiver.
findings.fix: Define h = +inf when the azimuth p->c lies outside the window's azimuth range, and take the minimum over all rules and windows. Evaluate each cell at its corner nearest p, or subtract a cell-size margin. For non-planar receivers, cast hulls per receiver sample elevation band. Add a fixture: a single-cell spike placed between two instants' azimuths must be caught.

findings.issue: The noise floor is defined as 'one raster cell area', but the compliance path is vector-based (Shapely hulls clipped to polygons). No raster or cell size is defined, so the floor is undefined in the main path.
findings.fix: State the floor as the receiver sample-grid cell (e.g. 0.5 m x 0.5 m = 0.25 m2), capped at 0.5% of the space area and 0 for 'no shadow' rules. Print it on every result.

findings.issue: There is no reachability pre-filter, although shadows only point 306-52 degrees (22 Sept) and 317-1 degrees (11 Nov). From most CBD blocks west of Cambie, the Victory Square cenotaph (S-SE of the CBD) cannot be reached by a morning shadow. The costly Stage B dual-reading work may therefore be irrelevant for most candidate blocks, and the effort is never triaged.
findings.fix: Precompute, for each candidate block, which Table-1 spaces fall inside the bearing wedge and reach. Show 'not reachable from this block' instead of running those rules, and use the result to order the remaining work.

findings.issue: The AGPL-3.0 decision is still open. M02, M03, M04, M07 and M08 all depend on Ladybug components, and only a 'proposed default' exists. Releasing a hosted service to entrants before the decision is made is a compliance risk.
findings.fix: Record the decision (platform under AGPL-3.0-or-later, or Ladybug calls in a separately published source-offering service) before any public release, and add the source link to the UI footer.

findings.issue: The claim that EPW stamps are local standard time is still unverified (S58 is silent), yet it shifts every occupancy schedule by one hour under BC's year-round UTC-7.
findings.fix: Open the EnergyPlus Input Output Reference or Engineering Reference section on weather-data time. Until then, keep the shared fixture test and show 'EPW time basis assumed LST' on M03, M04, M05 and M07 outputs.

false_assumptions.claim: The exception grounds 'affordable or social housing, major public amenities such as childcare, or city-building priorities' are a FALSE ASSUMPTION; the true list is social housing, below-market rental, public childcare, heritage conservation or a major city-building priority (3.1.2)
false_assumptions.why_false: The 'correction' rests on an unopened PDF relayed by a reviewer, while an opened secondary source that reports the approved text supports the original claim. Calling it false inverts the evidence hierarchy, and it also loses the Hotel Development Policy example, which matters for a tower with hotel programme.
false_assumptions.correction: Make it an UNVERIFIED conflict. Cite UDI for affordable or social housing, public childcare and city-building priorities such as the Hotel Development Policy (verified_secondary), and keep the relay-only items (below-market rental, heritage) as unverified. Section 6.2 (blanket 100% social-housing exemption) was removed.
false_assumptions.evidence: https://udi.org/advocacy/updates/city-of-vancouver-citywide-design-and-development-guidelines (opened 21 Oct 2026): 17 Sept 2025 entry lists case-by-case exceptions for 'affordable or social housing, major public amenities such as public childcare, and significant city-building priorities such as the Hotel Development Policy'; 'A motion to remove section 6.2' removed the 100% social housing exemption.

false_assumptions.claim: Victory Square being excluded from the CDDG area may change which document governs the cenotaph receiver after 27 Oct 2026
false_assumptions.why_false: The CDDG exclusion lists areas where the CDDG does not apply to applications, because area-specific policies continue there. It concerns the development site, not a protected receiver. A CBD tower site lies inside CDDG scope.
false_assumptions.correction: The CDDG governs the tower site. The open question is whether the posted CDDG solar chapter keeps the s.4.3.1 cenotaph protection; check it at the 13 Nov gate and ask cddg@vancouver.ca.
false_assumptions.evidence: https://vancouver.ca/home-property-development/city-wide-design-and-development-guidelines.aspx (opened 21 Oct 2026): 'The CDDG is intended to apply to most conditional development permit and rezoning applications city-wide. The CDDG does not apply in some areas where area-specific or site-specific policies and guidelines continue to apply, including ... Victory Square'; 'The final guidelines will be posted soon'; effective 27 Oct 2026.
